caption:
Every text, DM, and Slack ping - one single feed.

Back in 2023, a teenager's reverse-engineered app called Beeper Mini gave Android phones real blue-bubble iMessage: read receipts, typing indicators, all of it. Apple blocked it. Beeper patched around the block. Apple blocked it again. The back-and-forth ran for days and got covered by TechCrunch, The Verge, and the New York Times - it even has its own Wikipedia page.

Most people remember that news cycle and assume Beeper is either dead or still a hacky workaround. It's neither. It's now owned by Automattic (the company behind WordPress and Tumblr), and it just shipped Line integration, sticker packs, home-screen widgets, and a speed overhaul as recently as June 2026.

But the iMessage trick was never really the point. The actual reason to open Beeper today: it pulls WhatsApp, iMessage, Slack, Discord, Instagram DMs, Telegram, Signal, LinkedIn, and more into one searchable feed, synced across Mac, iPhone, Android, Windows, Linux, and ChromeOS. Long group chats get condensed into a summary, replies get drafted for you, and messages in other languages get translated on the spot.

Worth saying plainly: the original iMessage-on-Android trick isn't the guaranteed magic it once was - Apple's pushback made it unreliable, so Beeper now leans on relaying through a Mac you own. The unified inbox is the part that's rock solid.

Send this to whoever in your life still keeps six apps open just to check if anyone's talked to them, and save it so you don't lose it. Full breakdown - link in bio.
